title: Multi-File Graph Substrate
key_findings: A graph substrate can span multiple serialized files connected by cross-file edges
Writing a new file with a SUPERSEDES edge changes which graph governs execution
The original file is never modified — spawn-and-supersede is self-modification of the substrate, not of any individual file
Chained supersession (A→B→C) produces unbounded substrate growth with zero file modification
Single-file self-modification and spawn-and-supersede are functionally equivalent — both change the executing program during runtime
